title: Precision Slewing Kernel Gateway for dequant-latency control
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce a 'Precision Slewing Kernel Gateway' (PSKG) that acts as a lightweight arbitration layer between the request router and kernel executor to reduce dequant overhead on mixed-precision paths (INT8/FP8/FP16). PSKG dynamically selects a per-request precision lane, applies head/block-level slewing heuristics, and opportunistically bypasses dequant when cached KV or prefix heuristics indicate safe execution. Goal: reduce average decode latency by 8-20% for mixed-precision streaming workloads while preserving model quality and without large memory copies.
acceptance_criteria: PSKG integrated behind kernel selection API with config flag runtime.precision_slewing=true
End-to-end unit tests for precision-lane selection heuristics and dequant-bypass invariants
Benchmarked on production-like Llama-variants showing >=8% median decode latency reduction for mixed-precision streaming workloads at p95 load
No measurable quality regression on established eval prompt-set (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-assessments within noise)
Feature gated with canary rollout and telemetry to detect misroutes or increased error rates
design_notes: We avoid creating a separate heavy scheduler thread: PSKG is a thin sync decision layer that annotates request metadata for downstream kernel chooser.
Primary slewing signal is 'kv_reuse_score' computed from prefix cache hits and token frequency heuristics; fallback to sequence-length and temperature estimates.
Dequant bypass is allowed only when KV cache is hot and when the chosen kernel supports in-place mixed-precision accumulation to prevent correctness loss.
Prefer zero-copy reinterpret_cast paths where possible; when copying is unavoidable, amortize across microbatches and tag costs for telemetry.
Trade-off considered: aggressive bypass can reduce latency but risks small numerical drift; mitigation via conservative confidence thresholds and offline stress tests.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define PSKG proto annotations and integrate into request pipeline (router -> pskg -> kernel-chooser) (2 wks)
Phase 2: Implement slewing heuristics and dequant-bypass predicates with unit tests and property checks (2 wks)
Phase 3: Microbenchmark harness and perf tuning on INT8/FP8 builds across sequence lengths (1.5 wks)
Phase 4: Canary rollout for 5% of traffic with expanded telemetry, iterate on thresholds (1.5 wks)
Phase 5: Full rollout and documentation + runbook for rollback conditions (1 wk)
risks_and_mitigation: Numerical drift: add periodic evaluation hooks to re-run eval prompts in canary; revert if regression > noise threshold
Increased memory churn from mistaken zero-copy assumptions: add guard rails that detect incompatible allocator backends and fall back to safe copy
Heuristic misclassification under pathological workloads: expose override config and per-customer opt-out for private deployments
Telemetry volume: sample decision traces and only send aggregated histograms to avoid egress blowup
perf_results_summary: Local microbenchmarks (A100 + INT8 path) on 2048-token decode: median token latency down 12%, p95 down 9% when PSKG enabled with conservative thresholds
FP8 experiments show 8-15% end-to-end decode improvement depending on KV hit rate; benefits increase with prefix reuse
For pure FP16 workloads there's negligible difference (falls back to default kernel selection)
Memory overhead: additional metadata per request ~120 bytes; no persistent allocations introduced
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for all decision predicates and protobuf changes
Property tests simulating interleaved cached and uncached prefixes
A/B tests with canary traffic using traffic-generator harness on staging cluster
Offline eval harness against regression suite (1000 prompts) and new golden set for quantized drift detection
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated; enable on small internal tenant group first
Canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours with strict rollback on error-rate/latency anomalies
Increase to 25% for one week if stable, then 100%
Provide a kill-switch at router level to force 'no-slewing' if needed
